original_question: Does every Banach space of density greater than aleph_1 have a support set?
target_in_paper: Section 12, Problem 19: Todorcevic's variant of Rolewicz's support-set problem, namely 'Does every Banach space of density > ℵ_1 have a support set?'
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target almost verbatim: it asks about every Banach space, uses the threshold 'density greater than aleph_1', and asks for the existence of a support set. This matches the paper's official formulation in Section 12, Problem 19, rather than the broader earlier Rolewicz question about all non-separable Banach spaces.
missing_details: Replace informal 'density' by the density character, e.g. dens(X) > ℵ_1.
State the quantified ambient object explicitly: let X be a Banach space.
Define what a support set is in the paper's sense: a nonempty convex set C ⊆ X.
Define the support-point condition explicitly: for every x ∈ C there exists x* ∈ X* such that x*(x) = sup{ x*(y) : y ∈ C }.

To stay paper-faithful, note that this is the general Banach-space variant left open after the paper recalls Theorem 19 for C(K) spaces of density > ℵ_1; the draft itself does not mention that nearby narrowing/contrast.
refined_question: Let X be a Banach space with density character dens(X) > ℵ_1. Must there exist a nonempty convex set C ⊆ X such that every point x ∈ C is a support point of C; that is, for each x ∈ C there exists x* ∈ X* with x*(x) = sup{ x*(y) : y ∈ C }?
justification: The draft is aiming at the precise open problem recorded in Section 12 as Problem 19, not at the broader Problem 18. In that section the paper first defines support sets, recalls Rolewicz's original question asking which Banach spaces admit support sets and whether all non-separable Banach spaces do, then states Theorem 19 that every C(K) space of density > ℵ_1 has a support set, and immediately formulates the remaining open variant for arbitrary Banach spaces as Problem 19. So the nearest paper-faithful stand-alone sharpening is exactly the same question with the definitions of density character and support set made explicit.
